questions.q: In a DeepSpeed config, how is the effective per-replica batch size determined?
options: It is always fixed at 1 regardless of configuration
train_micro_batch_size_per_gpu multiplied by gradient_accumulation_steps gives the effective batch size per data-parallel replica
It is set entirely by the zero_optimization.stage field
It depends only on the number of GPUs, not the micro batch size
questions.explain: The per-GPU micro batch size times the number of gradient accumulation steps gives the effective batch size processed per replica before any weight update, which then multiplies further by replica count for the true global batch size.

questions.q: What does setting zero_optimization.stage to 3 in a DeepSpeed config accomplish?
options: It disables gradient computation
It shards parameters (in addition to gradients and optimizer state) across the data-parallel group, so no GPU holds the full model at rest
It increases the learning rate automatically
It switches training from bf16 to fp32
questions.explain: ZeRO stage 3 is the most aggressive sharding level, partitioning parameters as well as gradients and optimizer state, gathering them on demand rather than keeping full copies resident on every GPU.

questions.q: What is notably absent from the DeepSpeed JSON config walked through in this lesson, and why?
options: The learning rate, because DeepSpeed sets it automatically
Tensor-parallel and pipeline-parallel degree, because those are set as separate launch-time arguments in a Megatron-DeepSpeed-level configuration, not as fields in this DeepSpeed config
The batch size, because it is never configurable
The optimizer type, because DeepSpeed only supports one optimizer
questions.explain: This config assumes ZeRO-3 sharding and ordinary data parallelism only; tensor-parallel and pipeline-parallel degrees are a separate concern set at launch time in a larger Megatron-DeepSpeed-style configuration.

questions.q: How does the activation_checkpointing block in a DeepSpeed config relate to what was covered in Lesson 31?
options: It is unrelated -- DeepSpeed implements a completely different technique under this name
It turns on the same recompute-instead-of-store activation checkpointing technique as a config block, rather than requiring hand-wrapped torch.utils.checkpoint calls in the model code
It only applies to the optimizer state, not activations
It disables activation checkpointing by default and must be manually enabled elsewhere
questions.explain: DeepSpeed's activation_checkpointing config block enables the same discard-and-recompute technique described in Lesson 31, configured declaratively rather than via manual code wrapping.

questions.q: What does Chapter 6, previewed at the end of this lesson, focus on?
options: Choosing between LoRA and full fine-tuning
Keeping a long training run alive and observable: checkpointing, fault tolerance, mixed precision in more depth, and observability
Tokenization strategies for new languages
Prompt engineering techniques for inference
questions.explain: Chapter 5 covers getting a training job running across GPUs via parallelism; Chapter 6, ML Systems for Training, covers what keeps a long run alive and observable over days or weeks of training.
